title: Separate control-plane subnets and centralized NAT gateway for private control plane provisioning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: customer private control planes have mixed tenant/control traffic in the same subnets which complicates least-privilege security groups, egress cost accounting, and makes rolling upgrades riskier. This PR splits control-plane components into dedicated subnets and introduces an optional centralized NAT gateway pattern for control-plane egress, plus a small set of Terraform refactors to make the subnet layout pluggable.

What changed (high level):
- Terraform modules: refactor terraform/modules/vpc to support an explicit control_plane_subnets block and an optional centralized_nat boolean. When centralized_nat=true, we provision one NAT GW in a designated private subnet and route control-plane route tables to it.
- Route table & tagging: created a control-plane-specific route table resource, with automated route propagations and strong tags (kubernetes.io/cluster, redwood:control-plane).
- Security groups: introduced redwood_control_plane_sg which is minimal (control-plane ports only) and used by API, controller, and metrics collectors. Documented required security group rules in MODULES.md.
- Interface endpoints: moved interface endpoint creation into a conditional module call so private-installers do not create endpoints for AWS accounts that prefer centralized endpoints. Added endpoint_type variable (Interface|Gateway) and explicit vpc_endpoint_policy override.
- DNS/delegation: added optional private-hosted-zone delegation for control-plane.<control-zone> to enable split-horizon routing. This uses route53 zone delegation outputs if cross-account delegation is enabled.
- Helm chart: small values/defaults added (controlPlane.subnetSelector, controlPlane.useCentralizedNat) so installer chart can set subnet allocation for control plane components.
- Rollback: added a migration plan in docs/upgrade.md that describes safe sequence to flip traffic and remove shared NATs.

Backward compatibility & rollout:
- Default behavior preserves current layout (centralized_nat=false and control_plane_subnets omitted) so existing installs do not change. Enabling the feature requires plan/apply and a documented cutover (move controllers to new subnets, update SG references).
- Migration helpers: terraform plan output includes a helper script (scripts/collect-sg-mappings.sh) to generate the mapping for resources that need to switch security groups.

Testing & validation:
- unit: terraform validate + module unit tests (mocks) run in CI.
- infra e2e: deployed to a dedicated test account with centralized_nat=true, ran smoke tests for control-plane connectivity, and validated DNS delegation across two accounts.
- perf: minor improvement in egress cost visibility (separates NAT flow logs from tenant egress).

Notes: see release_notes for operator actions required during upgrade. The PR intentionally keeps the feature gated behind variables to avoid surprise changes to existing installations.
commits: 6 commits: refactor(vpc-module): add control_plane_subnets and centralized_nat toggle; feat(terraform): add control-plane route table and tags; feat(security): create redwood_control_plane_sg and update module outputs; docs: MODULES.md + upgrade checklist; helm: values for controlPlane subnetSelector and centralizedNat; ci: add terraform-module unit tests
review_comments: Arjun: Can we avoid creating NAT GW when AZs > 1 and customers have an existing shared NAT? Suggest a var allow_shared_nat with an id input.
Maya: Added allow_shared_nat and a shared_nat_id input. If provided, we skip NAT creation and attach route to the provided NAT. Documented in MODULES.md.
Lena: Security review: confirm control-plane SG does not allow outbound 0.0.0.0/0 on admin ports. Also request an explicit ingress rule list rather than open ephemeral ranges.
Maya: tightened SG rules, swapped ephemeral ranges to only allow node-port egress where required. Updated unit tests to assert ports. PTAL.
Samir: CI flaky e2e failed once due to delayed route propagation; added a retry with backoff in the smoke test and an infrastructure note on route table propagation timing.
Lena: Approved after SG changes and docs updated.
Arjun: Approved. Squash-merge looks good; please include a short migration appendix in release notes.
release_notes: Operator action required (optional): To enable separated control-plane subnets and centralized NAT, set module variable control_plane_subnets and centralized_nat=true in your installer config. If you use a shared NAT, set shared_nat_id to avoid provisioning a new NAT gateway. Migration steps are documented in docs/upgrade.md (follow sequence: provision subnets -> migrate controllers -> swap SG references -> decommission old paths).
regression_risks: low: feature gated by variables. Medium risk during manual migration if SG references are missed. Tests added to CI to catch common misconfigurations.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in production, allow for up to 5 minutes per route table change for propagation and verify control-plane DNS delegation before switching traffic. Collect SG mapping with scripts/collect-sg-mappings.sh to expedite cutover.
acknowledgements: Thanks to infra on-call (Samir) for test account access and to product for specifying cost-accounting requirements.
notes: This PR focuses on control-plane isolation and egress accounting; a follow-up will add optional flow logs export and a small UI toggle in the console for installers created via the dashboard.
